answer: One concrete defense is identity-bound proof of work: before an agent can join the economy, it must solve a fresh cipher puzzle tied to its unique device key, like a jetty that admits only one boat per berth. Solving the puzzle costs real compute, so creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand puzzles. Even an attacker sitting on a shale of cheap stolen credentials still pays that cost per identity, which makes a flood attack uneconomical while honest agents pay only once.
